To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Hippo and the Small Gtpase pathways regulate YAP/TAz activity by regulating its DNA binding transcription factor.
small GTPASE pathways activate YAP and TAZ, while the Hippopotamus pathway inhibits them.
the Hippo pathway is a master inhibitor of the small GTPase pathway and that YAP/TA2 are transducers of the cell structural and mechanical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of YPA/TAZ by cell structural and environmental factors.
the regulation of the YAP/TAZE protein by the Hippo and small GTPases pathways.
the reciprocal regulation of the Hippo pathway by small GTPases, and of small GTPases by the Hippo pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
YAP/TA2 are the central integrators of cell shape and cytoskeletal dynamics.
YAP/TA2 is regulated by the Hippo and the small GTPase pathway, and that these pathways are intimately connected.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hippo pathway is a master inhibitor of YAP/TEAD signaling, and small GTPases are a master activator of YAP/Runx3 signaling.
YAP/TAz are regulated by the Hippo and small GTPases pathways, and the balance of these pathways determines whether YAP/TA2 are activated or not.
small GTPasess activate YAP/TEAD and the Hippo pathway activates YAP/RUNX3, while YAP/TAz can also regulate small GTPases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the YAP/TAz response to cell shape and microenvironment is mediated by the Hippo and small GTPases pathways.
the YAP/TAz response to cell shape, cell polarity, and cell-ECM interactions depends on the Hippo and small GTPases pathways.
small GTPasses are important regulators of the YAP/TAz transcriptional activity, and that they do so by modulating the DNA-binding transcription factors that bind to YAP/TA2.
